subject: science
passage: Crushed waste glass can replace some of the sand in concrete, which keeps glass out of landfills. Civil engineer Hana Novak made concrete samples in which 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, or 40% of the sand was replaced with glass and measured the pressure each sample could withstand after 28 days. She found that replacing up to 20% of the sand had little effect on strength, but that ______

data.title: Strength of Concrete Made with Crushed Glass in Place of Sand

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.A: the concrete with 10% glass was slightly stronger than the concrete with no glass.
choices.B: strength dropped to about 35 megapascals at 30% glass and to about 31 at 40%.
choices.C: the concrete with 40% glass cost less to produce than the concrete with no glass.
choices.D: strength rose steadily as more glass was added, reaching its highest point at 40%.

explanation.why: "But" signals a contrast with "little effect on strength" up to 20%, so the blank must describe a clear loss of strength at higher amounts of glass. Strength stays near 40 megapascals up to 20% glass, then falls to 35.1 at 30% and 30.6 at 40%.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is true (40.8 versus 40.2), but it describes the range where glass had little effect and does not provide the contrast that "but" requires.
explanation.B: Correct. Beyond 20%, strength fell clearly, to about 35 and then about 31 megapascals, which contrasts with the small changes at lower amounts.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The table gives no information about cost.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This reverses the trend: the 40% sample was the weakest in the table, not the strongest.
